chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not for the sick man that he divorces, but for him is that he can marry.
ai.seo_question: Can a sick person divorce or remarry according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recorded in *Al-Kafi*, the Imam clarifies that physical illness does not impair a man's legal capacity (*ahliyyah*) for marriage or divorce, distinguishing it from conditions like insanity or unconsciousness. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of marital acts performed by the sick, emphasizing that the mere presence of disease does not nullify the power of attorney over one's spouse. It reflects the practical application of general principles of capacity, ensuring that temporary physical ailments do not inadvertently alter family law status.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not for the sick that he divorces but for him is that he can marry’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One cannot divorce his wife in his illness but his marriage is permissible.’”
